sponsors: Rep. Justin Slaughter and House co-sponsors; Senate sponsors Lakesia Collins and Doris Turner
status: Passed House 114-1-0 on 2025-04-10; arrived in Senate, assigned to Executive Committee, deadline extended, then re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2025-06-02; no action recorded since
key_provisions: Engrossed proposal requires U.S. processing, storage and disposal of defined state data under covered storage contracts unless the chief procurement officer authorizes otherwise, with exclusions including primarily telecommunications contracts. Credits earned after qualifying contract completion favor Illinois and qualified-area storage for future bids; qualifying data-center RFPs also receive location preference points.

status: Filed 2026-01-07; first reading and referred to House Rules Committee 2026-01-14; no further action recorded
key_provisions: Introduced proposal creates a compensation framework for qualifying property within 1,000 feet of a data center when construction or operation materially and proximately causes specified measurable harm, including property-value or business-revenue loss and qualifying adverse impacts. It provides appraisal and civil-remedy procedures and limits concurrent home-rule powers; proximity alone does not establish compensation eligibility.

bill: HB5513 (Hyperscale Data Centers / POWER Act companion)
sponsors: Rep. Robyn Gabel with multiple House Democratic co-sponsors
status: Assigned to Executive Committee 2026-02-24; re-referred to House Rules Committee under Rule 19(a) on 2026-03-27. The retained action table lists co-sponsor additions through 2026-10-23; this sponsor-action date is distinct from the last substantive re-referral. Later disposition was not independently established by this review.
key_provisions: House companion to SB4016 with environmental, water, energy, public-benefit, reporting, and solar permitting provisions.

sponsors: Sen. Sue Rezin; co-sponsors Sally J. Turner and Terri Bryant
status: Referred to Senate Assignments Committee 2025-01-17; co-sponsors added 2025-04-03; no action recorded in 2026
key_provisions: Introduced Data Center Construction by Foreign Adversaries Act would bar construction by a foreign company unless ICC, IPA and DCEO jointly study consumption and certify the specified self-generated-load and PJM/MISO conditions. The definition includes an entity at least 51% owned by a foreign adversary or headquartered in a country governed by one.

status: Moved to Executive Committee 2026-01-27; to AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-04; amendment filed 2026-03-31; committee deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; bill and amendment re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22
key_provisions: Creates Illinois Data Center Energy and Water Reporting Act; annual energy and water reporting to IPA; IPA ratepayer-impact study; confidentiality, public access, enforcement, and penalties.

sponsors: Sen. Mark L. Walker; co-sponsors Chris Balkema and Robert Peters
status: Assigned to Senate Revenue Committee 2025-03-04; committee/3rd reading deadline extended to 2025-06-01; re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2025-06-02; no action recorded in 2026
key_provisions: Expands the state data center definition for incentive purposes to include a quantum research facility.

status: To AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-18; committee deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22
key_provisions: Conditions data center incentive qualification on water stewardship strategy disclosure and requires DCEO reporting on recipient water stewardship strategies.

status: To AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-25; Rule 2-10 deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22
key_provisions: Establishes data center self-direct clean energy program, 180-day preconstruction disclosure to ICC, public meeting requirements, water-use disclosures to DNR, penalties up to $10,000 per violation, and utility tariff review.

status: To AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-25; Amendment No. 2 filed 2026-04-27; Rule 2-10 deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; bill and both amendments re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22
key_provisions: Similar clean energy self-direct and utility tariff framework; adds water discharge pollutant identification, DNR water-use disclosure, Water Use Act changes, and groundwater emergency provisions.

status: To AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-25; Rule 2-10 deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; Senate Committee Amendment No. 1 filed 2026-05-05; bill and amendment re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22; co-sponsors added through 2026-09-02 (Latest sponsor-action date is distinct from the last substantive re-referral.)
key_provisions: Creates Data Center Water Transparency and Aquifer Protection Act; bars data centers from using Mahomet Aquifer water beginning 2027; bars permits for Mahomet withdrawals; requires existing users to transition by 2028; bans local nondisclosure clauses restricting water-use disclosure.

sponsors: Sen. Ram Villivalam with chief co-sponsors Robert Peters, Graciela Guzman, and Rachel Ventura, plus additional co-sponsors
status: To AI and Social Media Committee 2026-02-25; Rule 2-10 deadline chain extended 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-24 to 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-22; re-referred to Senate Assignments Committee (Rule 3-9(a)) 2026-05-22; co-sponsors added through 2026-05-30
key_provisions: Comprehensive hyperscale data center regulation: cumulative impact review, public notice, community benefit agreements, NDA restrictions, water-impact permits, quarterly water reporting, water scarcity plans, energy and water reporting to ICC, hyperscale self-direct program, funds supported by annual fees based on peak demand, labor and equity provisions.
